title: Mud Carey, Jack, and Blind Charlie
summary: Brief recollections of Mud Carey, his brother Jack, and Blind Charlie, whom he taught saxophone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I knew him. He played with Ory out in California.
Yeah, we played right here and he used to play right there too.
I never knew his brother Jack the trombone band.

Jack used to play trombone. I played with Blind Charlie. A fella called Blind Charlie. He played, he played clarinet, he played piano. He played, he didn't play no saxophone, but clarinet, he played piano. He played guitar. You know what all that means, you know.
He played with Louie Dumaine. He might have heard him with Louie.

He played with Amos Riley, uptown Amos Riley. And so he could take his watch out, the face was broke. So come on, we ain't got about a minute to catch this call. Come on, we got one minute. When he feel like watch the face was open, you could tell the time. I learned a little blind boy, he was sitting there how to play, not clarinet, I learned him how to play saxophone. And he was out in Baton Rouge, he was going to school and he was a great clarinet player. I called him Sidney. Good saxophone player. I know about clarinet, but he got him a clarinet anyhow. He'd play around the boy up on the street so I haven't heard no more about him. He might be dead too. But all those fellas were good musicians around here. The best band named Piro Sapiro's band, those bands was bang. Those were great days. Yeah. Uh-oh.
